- **Gruber & Söhne** (row 6 removed; the email differs only in case)
- **Pichler Elektro** (row 20 removed)
- **Café Lindner** (row 26 removed)
- **Bauer IT** (row 27 removed)

- **Anna Berger** (row 33 removed; the email had a trailing space)
- **Müller GmbH** (row 32 "Mueller GmbH" removed; same email as the row kept, but the spelling of the name differs)

The last one is a judgment call. If you want matching by name as well as email, "Mueller GmbH" should stay, which would leave 32 customers.

L2.title: Precise prompt
L2.prompt: Remove duplicate customers from kunden.csv and save the result as bereinigt.csv. Two rows are the same customer if the e-mail is the same, ignoring upper and lower case and spaces at the edges. How many customers are left? Reply in English.

lines.text:
1	Name;E-Mail;Ort
2	Gasthaus Brunner;tisch@gasthaus-brunner.at;Bad Ischl
3	Gruber & Söhne;Office@Gruber.at;Steyr
… (39 more lines)
File created successfully at: .\bereinigt.csv (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)

There are **31 customers** left.

I removed 9 duplicate rows from the 40 in `kunden.csv`, keeping the first occurrence of each e-mail (matched case-insensitively, with edge spaces trimmed). The removed rows were 6, 17, 20, 26, 27, 31, 32, 33 and 34. Row 33 (`anna.berger@mail.at `, with a trailing space) matched row 23.

The result is saved as `bereinigt.csv` in the same folder. I kept the header and the original capitalisation of the kept rows. The file was written as UTF-8 with LF line endings, so if the original used CRLF or a BOM, the new file will differ in that respect.
